paper_title: Lattice QCD input for axion cosmology
coupling_convention: f_a in GeV (x-axis), m_a in eV (y-axis)
notes: Paper presents a lattice QCD calculation of the temperature-dependent axion mass via topological susceptibility χ(T). The primary result is a lower bound on axion mass m_a ≥ (14.6 ± 0.1) μeV corresponding to an upper bound on the decay constant f_a ≤ (4.10 ± 0.04) × 10^11 GeV for the post-inflation PQ-breaking scenario using the misalignment mechanism. This is derived from pure Yang-Mills (SU(3)) lattice calculations at high temperatures (T/Tc ~ 1.2-2.5), extrapolated via DIGM fits to extract the characteristic temperature T1 where m_a ~ 3H. The bound is mass-independent in the sense that it constrains the f_a-m_a relation via Eq. (3): m_a f_a = √(m_u m_d)/(m_u + m_d) × f_π m_π. Encoded as two-point horizontal line spanning the viable f_a range. Key limitations: (1) pure-glue calculation without dynamical fermions; (2) critical temperature T_c differs by factor ~2 from QCD; (3) does not include string/domain wall contributions. Confidence is 0.75 rather than higher because: (a) the paper explicitly states results are preliminary and not yet applicable to realistic experiments due to pure-glue approximation; (b) coupling type is unambiguous (AxionMass) but the bound itself carries significant uncontrolled systematics from omitted fermion effects; (c) the numerical result is well-defined and clearly stated in Eq.
